compiled_state.title: [sprint/create-sprint-draft-pr]: ci-pr Phase A opens a draft PR base=main head=session -> non-conforming session->main PR
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## 2. Incident Overview

**Scenario Type:** User-flagged process non-conformance.

### Expected Behavior
The session worktree should reach main only through the conforming promotion path (merge-to-main.sh: source -> staged-* PR1 with review-sub-pr, staged-* -> main PR2 with llm-review; or the MQ model under MQ-4). No standalone draft PR that proposes a direct session-worktree -> main merge should exist.

### Actual Behavior
sprint Phase A (ci-pr mode) calls create-sprint-draft-pr.sh, which runs `gh pr create --draft --base $_DEFAULT_BRANCH(main) --head $SESSION_BRANCH` (create-sprint-draft-pr.sh:113-116; also :46,:62). This opens a long-lived DRAFT PR proposing session-worktree -> main. Its stated purpose is to be the GitHubPRDefenseStore substrate (a PR to attach per-story review defenses to), but as a base=main/head=session PR it (a) implies a direct session->main merge our process does not perform, (b) lingers alongside the staged-tier PRs that actually carry promotion, and (c) would bypass staged review if marked ready.

### Open scoping question (for triage)
This overlaps MQ-4 (40f7-e831-b9e8-4158), which rewrites the promotion path to 'session->main direct' through the merge queue and retires the staged-*/PR1/PR2 tiers. Under MQ-4 a session->main PR becomes the REAL promotion PR (through the queue), which may SUBSUME this umbrella draft PR. Decision needed: fix standalone now (e.g., point the defense substrate at the conforming PR, or stop opening a base=main draft) vs. fold into MQ-4's promotion-path rewrite.

### Affected files
plugins/dso/scripts/create-sprint-draft-pr.sh; plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md (Phase A Draft PR Creation, ~line 175-192).

**code_version:** 2bb8ef2bebc9601df9580196a77e23ca0bd68966

comments.body: THIRD HARM (concrete, from live session diagnosis) — strengthens the fix toward removing base=main: the umbrella draft PR (base=main, head=session) makes check-staged-head (a required check scoped 'on: pull_request: branches:[main]') RUN on the shared session HEAD commit. check-staged-head enforces 'only staged-* heads may target main'; the umbrella's head is the session worktree branch (not staged-*), so it HARD-FAILS. GitHub attaches that failing check-run to the commit SHA, and because PR1 (session->staged, e.g. #558) shares the same head SHA, the failing status CONTAMINATES PR1 -> merge-to-main treats it as a terminal required-check failure and refuses to advance. So the umbrella PR being base=main is not merely confusing the resume fallback — it ACTIVELY BREAKS promotion via shared-commit status contamination. IMPLICATION: filtering the resume open-PR fallback to ignore the umbrella (option i) is INSUFFICIENT; the contamination happens independent of resume. The 1f5f fix must prevent the umbrella from being base=main (option ii — relocate the GitHubPRDefenseStore substrate / stop opening a base=main draft), OR scope check-staged-head to the actual promotion PR. This is now the strongest evidence that the umbrella PR is the linchpin of the whole cascade.
comments.author: Test

comments.body: FIX IMPLEMENTED + committed (bace2dc4ba): check-staged-head passes draft PRs (the umbrella is always a draft) so its failure no longer contaminates PR1's shared head SHA; ready_for_review added to triggers to close the draft->ready bypass. Enforcement intact (non-draft non-staged still blocks). Behavioral test 5/5. Combined with Fix C (resume fallback excludes base=main umbrella) in 78163b1407, all three 1f5f harms are now addressed. Landing on branch fix/merge-to-main-resume-hardening.
